newsitem.title: ISRAEL: No Hebron handover before Thursday, Israel says.
newsitem.headline: No Hebron handover before Thursday, Israel says.

text.p: Israel's Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai has ordered the army to wait until parliament approves the Hebron deal before handing over the West Bank town to Palestinian self-rule, his spokesman said on Wednesday.
The 120-seat parliament is expected to vote on the deal late on Thursday.

"Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai today ordered the Israel Defence Forces (IDF) and the security establishment not to begin the actual redeployment in Hebron until the Hebron agreement is approved by the Knesset, which is due to convene tomorrow," his spokesman said in a statement.

But Mordechai did authorise the removal of heavy equipment and other preliminary measures once the agreement is approved by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's cabinet in a vote expected late on Wednesday.

"Mordechai ordered that the redeployment be carried out with minimal friction, by refraining -- as much as possible -- from disturbing the daily lives of Hebron's Jewish and Arab residents. He also directed that the redeployment not violate the (Jewish) sabbath," the statement said.
"Large IDF forces are ready to carry out the redeployment according to whatever timetable is approved by the defence minister," the statement said.
